Class PlayerSlotCapture

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.attachment.PlayerSlotCapture
public final class PlayerSlotCapture extends Object
§0052 Phase 2 — the grave-capture surface. Generic over every death-droppable MKC player content slot (the PLAYER_DEATH_DROP registry). A grave-mod adapter captures (reads + clears) the slots into the grave's data and restores them on collect by calling this surface — never individual slots. So an adapter is write-once-per-grave-mod; every consumer's slots (Pockets, Equipment, future) ride the same adapter for free.

Ordering: grave mods capture before vanilla drops the inventory (Universal Graves injects ahead of dropEquipment), so captureAndClear(ServerPlayer) runs upstream of the Phase-1 dropEquipment floor — the floor then finds the slots empty and drops nothing. No dupes, no explicit suppression. The clear here is the same write-back-empty Phase 1 uses; respawn's copyOnDeath then carries an empty bag.

  • Method Details

    • captureAndClear

      public static List<PlayerSlotCapture.CapturedSlot> captureAndClear(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player)
      For every death-droppable player content slot on player, read the non-empty stack and CLEAR the slot. Returns the captured slots for the adapter to push into the grave. Clearing makes the Phase-1 floor stand down (it finds the slots empty). Server-side.

    • restore

      public static boolean restore(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player, PlayerSlotCapture.CapturedSlot slot)
      Writes a captured stack back to its slot on grave collect. No-ops (returns false) if the attachment id is unknown or the index is out of range — the slot layout changed since capture (consumer reconfigured / removed the attachment); the caller handles such overflow (e.g. drops it).
      Returns:
      true if restored to the slot; false if it couldn't be placed

    • restoreAll

      public static List<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack> restoreAll(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player, List<PlayerSlotCapture.CapturedSlot> slots)
      Restores a whole capture; returns the stacks that could NOT be placed (unknown attachment / out-of-range index) so the caller can drop them.
